## 3. Construction concept

### 3.1 The two systems

Two separate timber systems, as in the red building (photo rule 2): a self-supporting boarded box, and an exoskeleton of 11 ring trusses standing 0.08 m outside it. The box carries its own floor, walls and roof to the raft. The trusses carry themselves and brace the box; the box is tied to the truss legs at every rail level. Keeping them separate is what lets the trusses ripple while the inside stays a plain box, and it avoids the collision a shared roof would cause (webs rising from a chord that also carries a deck).

### 3.2 Slat family (mine, to be checked by the Researcher; section 4 records the verdict)

Two sections only, both thin, no other timber in the model:

- F, framing slat, 30 x 120 mm: studs, rails, plates, joists, chords, webs, braces, deck boards of the roof, door ledges.
- B, board, 24 x 120 mm: wall boards inside and out, floor boards, door boards.

Capacity comes from repetition, never from a bigger section: paired slats face to face for studs and joists (60 x 120), paired slats with webs between them for truss chords (the sandwich of photo rule 2 and Erne). Slat length 4.80 m maximum; in a pair the two slats' splices are staggered by half a length; splices land on a support or a node. Nailed and bolted throughout, no carved joints.

### 3.3 Bearing stack, ground to roof

1. Raft: concrete, 7.20 x 7.20 x 0.25 m, top face at z = 0, centred (mine; the one non-timber element, it stands in for the ground). Truss legs stand on it in steel shoes with hold-down bolts (named, not modelled). Wall bottom plates lie on it.
2. Floor: joists = paired F on edge (60 wide x 120 deep), running x from x = -2.004 to +2.004 (stud face to stud face; the inner lining starts on top of the floor), at y = -1.95 + 0.65 k, k = 0..6 (7 joists, on the 0.65 module shared with the studs and the trusses). Floor boards B laid flat across the joists, running y, from y = -2.004 to +2.004 and x = -2.004 to +2.004, no gaps. Floor top z = 0.144 = 0.120 joist + 0.024 board.
3. Walls: four walls, 0.228 m thick, room clear 3.90 (inner board faces at +/-1.950). Build-up from inside, distances from the plan centre: inner boards B 24 (1.950 to 1.974), inner rails F 30 laid with the 30 through the wall (1.974 to 2.004), stud zone 120 (2.004 to 2.124, stud centreline 2.064), outer rails F 30 (2.124 to 2.154), outer boards B 24 (2.154 to 2.178). Outer face at 2.178. Studs = paired F face to face (60 x 120) on the 0.65 module: side walls (normal x) at y = 0, +/-0.65, +/-1.30, +/-1.95, plus an end stud at each end of each wall; end walls (normal y) at x = 0 (removed at the door), +/-0.65, +/-1.30, +/-1.95, plus end studs. Side walls run through in y, end walls fit between them. Bottom plate F flat, 30 x 120, on the raft under the stud zone. Rails on both faces at z centres 0.65 k for k = 1..14, a bottom rail (inner: 0.144 to 0.264 on the floor; outer: 0.000 to 0.120 on the raft), and a sill rail 9.51 to 9.63 under the top of the boards. Boards vertical, 24 x 120, from the bottom rail to z = 9.63, lengths at most 4.80, joints on rail centres, adjacent boards alternate two joint patterns (A: joints at 3.25 and 7.15; B: joints at 1.95 and 5.85) so no two neighbours share a joint (photo rule 6).
4. Band: above z = 9.63 the studs continue as bare mullions to the head; a head rail F on both faces directly under the head plate. Nothing between mullions (glass not modelled).
5. Wall heads. Side walls: level head plate F flat, top at z_h = z_e - 0.37 (expected 11.53; see 3.6 for z_e). End walls: gable walls, studs cut to the slope, sloped head plate F under the roof deck, top face on the deck underside plane (3.3.6); the end walls carry the deck edge directly.
6. Box roof: 7 shallow slat trusses at y = 0, +/-0.65, +/-1.30, +/-1.95, over the studs (vertical alignment, one module). Each: bottom chord paired F sandwich (30 + 60 gap + 30 = 120 thick, 120 deep) level on the side wall head plates from x = -2.124 to +2.124 (the stud zone); two top chords, same sandwich, at 1:6 from the heel to the apex at x = 0, the top chord's underside passing through the bottom chord's top outer arris at x = +/-2.124 (arris bearing); webs F single: a king post at x = 0, queen posts at x = +/-1.06, two diagonals from the bottom chord's centre node up to the top chords at x = +/-1.06. Deck: F 30 x 120 laid flat, running y across the trusses (span 0.65), from y = -2.28 to +2.28 (one piece each), on both slopes from the eave at x = +/-2.28 to the apex, touching, the last board ripped. Deck underside plane (the top chords' top face, extended): z = z_h + 0.242 + (2.124 - |x|) / 6. Deck top at the eave edge (x = 2.28) z_h + 0.246, at the apex z_h + 0.626. Boards laid across the trusses and nailed at every chord act as the roof diaphragm together with the box; covering and drainage are not modelled (brief: no sheet material); the 1:6 fall to both eaves is what a membrane would need.
7. Ring trusses, the outer structure: 11 planes at y_i = -3.25 + 0.65 i, i = 0..10. See 3.6.
8. Door: opening 1.00 wide x 2.10 tall through all wall layers, centred at x = 0 in the -y wall, sill at the floor (z = 0.144), head at z = 2.244. Framing in the stud zone: king studs at x = +/-0.65 (the module studs), jacks doubled inside them (2 x 60 = 120 each side) to bring the module opening down to 1.00; header of four F on edge side by side (120 x 120) on the jacks from z = 2.244 to 2.364; cripples above at the module up to the head. Rails and boards on both faces stop at the opening. Leaf: ledged and braced, B boards vertical on three F ledges (at 0.25, 1.05 and 1.85 above the sill) and two F braces (each from the hinge side of a lower ledge to the free side of the ledge above), 1.00 x 2.10 x 0.054, hung on the +x jamb, modelled open 90 degrees into the room (brace direction and size ranges from the external row in section 4).

### 3.5 Lateral system, per direction

- Across the trusses (x): each ring truss is a portal whose corners are trussed (chords continuous around the eave, webs continue), so the 11 rings are 11 moment frames. The box's side walls are tied to the legs at every rail (bolts through the outer boards into the leg's inner chord, named, not modelled). Load path: wind on a side wall -> studs -> rails -> ties -> ring legs -> trussed corners and feet -> raft.
- Along the row (y): the rings are thin planes and need bracing between them. Diagonal braces F 30 x 120 in the gap between the box and the legs, lying flat against the legs' inner faces, in the plane x = +/-(2.198 to 2.228). Per side four X's in four panels: y from -3.25 to 0 and from 0 to 3.25, z from 0.15 to 5.95 and from 6.05 to 11.75; each X is the two diagonals of its panel (corner to corner), so 8 diagonals per side, 16 in all, each about 6.65 m long at 61 degrees to the horizontal (CMHC Fig. 86 and FRIM Fig. 30 both want braces at 45 degrees or steeper; one X across the whole row would sit at 42 degrees, which is why the panels are half the row). Halving joint where the two diagonals of an X cross (three boxes, as in the timber-framing skill); each diagonal spliced once at a leg crossing (4.80 + rest), the splice landing on a leg. Horizontal ties F in the same plane at z = 5.95 to 6.07 and z = 11.75 to 11.87 from y = -3.25 to 3.25 (FRIM Table 1 item E2, horizontal brace tying trussed frames). Every diagonal and tie is nailed to every leg it crosses (named, not modelled). Load path: wind on an end wall -> end wall studs -> box roof deck (boards nailed at every chord act as the diaphragm) and the rails -> side walls -> ties to the legs -> braced planes -> feet -> raft. The braced planes reach the eave, so they serve the whole height.
- The box itself: boards nailed to rails and studs on both faces make each wall a shear panel; the floor is on the raft.

### 3.6 The ring trusses and the ripple rule

Plane thickness 120 mm: chord slats at y_i - 0.060 to -0.030 and +0.030 to +0.060; webs in two planes, rising webs at y_i - 0.030 to 0.000, falling webs at 0.000 to +0.030, so the two webs meeting at a node never share a plane. Chord slats F 30 x 120 with the 120 in the truss plane; webs F 30 x 120 likewise.

Inner outline (chord centreline), the same for every truss: (-2.32, 0) -> (-2.32, z_e) -> (0, z_e + 0.387) -> (2.32, z_e) -> (2.32, 0). The 1:6 gable matches the box roof. Inner chord inner face at 2.26, i.e. 0.082 outside the wall face (2.178), room for the y-braces. The inner chord's underside clears the box deck top by about 0.06 at the eave and the apex when z_h = z_e - 0.37.

Arc length s along the inner outline from the left foot (s = 0) to the right foot (s = 2 z_e + 4.704). Truss depth, centreline to centreline, measured along the outward normal:

    d(s, i) = 0.63 + 0.30 * sin(2 * pi * s / 8.0 + 2 * pi * i / 11)      i = 0..10

so d runs from 0.33 to 0.93 m (mine: Erne's trusses are about a metre deep; 0.33 is the least depth that keeps the webs steeper than 40 degrees at a 0.8 m panel). Wavelength 8.0 m along the outline: about 1.5 waves per leg and a little over half a wave across the top, an arc rather than a crenellation. Phase advance 1/11 of a turn per truss: the crest travels one full wavelength across the row, adjacent trusses differ by at most 0.17 m, and the crests run diagonally across the side elevations as in the Tschumi image.

Nodes: inner nodes at the four corners of the outline plus equal subdivisions of every straight run into panels of at most 0.80 m (legs: 15 panels; each half of the top: 3 panels). Outer vertices at every half-panel position and at both feet: Q(s) = P(s) + n(s) d(s, i), n the outward unit normal of the run the point lies on. The outer chord is the polyline through the outer vertices, one straight sandwich pair per segment, consecutive segments mitred on the bisector plane at their shared vertex; the corners of the outline are therefore chamfered by the outer chord, not mitred. Webs: a Warren zigzag, inner node -> next outer vertex -> next inner node, alternating planes, ends inset so no corner crosses the far face of the chord it lands in. Both chords reach z = 0 at each foot.

Overall size rule (brief): W_out = the larger of the plan extents of the outer structure over slat faces (x: outer chord faces at the deepest point, expected 2 x 3.31 = 6.62; y: end truss faces, 2 x 3.31 = 6.62); H_out = highest slat face of the outer chords; H_out = 2.00 x W_out within 1 percent. The Builder measures both on the generated geometry and tunes z_e (expected 11.90) until the ratio holds; z_h follows as z_e - 0.37. Nothing else moves.

### 3.7 Estimated piece count (mine)

Ring trusses about 11 x 162 = 1780; box about 1400 (studs and splices 170, rails 140, boards 660, floor 50, roof trusses 100, deck 80, door 20, plates and heads 20); braces and ties 20. About 3200 pieces. If the render or check loop cannot carry it, the first reduction is the panel length 0.80 -> 1.00 (about 1450 truss pieces); the count of trusses and the module stay.

## 4. Rules from the Researcher

Verdict table and rows in `Fable/sources.md`; snippets in `references/` (named `manual_<manual>_p<page>_<what>.png`, captions in `references/captions.md`). What the Builder needs from them is here.

Confirmed (the concept stands):

- Floor board B 24 at 0.65 m joist spacing: CMHC Table 22 (p. 287) minimum lumber subfloor 19 mm at 600 mm; FRIM Table 1 A7 floor board 22 x 145 at 610 mm centres. Conservative.
- Roof deck F 30 flat at 0.65 m truss spacing: CMHC Table 35 (p. 305) minimum lumber roof sheathing 19 mm at 600 mm. Conservative. Boards up to 184 wide get 2 nails per support (CMHC Table 23), named.
- Roof heel: the bottom chord bears directly over the wall on the head plate, the top chord seated on the bottom chord's arris (CMHC Fig. 86, p. 125, heel bearing over the exterior wall plate; FRIM Sheet 9 shallow gable truss on a wall plate).
- 1:6 pitch: exactly CMHC's threshold for low-slope covering (Table 36, p. 306); at or below it a full membrane is required. Covering not modelled (brief); the note stands in the deviation table.
- Door opening: CMHC p. 109 and APA p. 15-16 both need only a single jack per side at 1.0 m; the doubled jacks are for opening size (module 1.12 -> 1.00), not for load. Kept.
- Diagonal braces at 45 degrees or steeper (CMHC Fig. 86; FRIM Ch. 6 p. 41, Fig. 30): the y-bracing panels were halved to 3.25 m wide so the X's stand at 61 degrees (section 3.5). Horizontal ties between trussed frames: FRIM Table 1 E2.
- Built-up members: nail from each side, rows at most 450 mm apart, end nails 100 to 150 mm from the ends (CMHC p. 94); splices in a pair staggered and plated (FRIM Sheet 7 bearer splice 2/30 x 194 x 440 bolted at 110). Named, not modelled; the geometry rule (splices staggered, on a support or node) is in 3.2.
- Truss feet: post in a steel U-strap (6 x 100) with 2 bolts 12.7 mm on a concrete footing (FRIM Sheet 7, PDF p. 56). Named, not modelled. FRIM wants the footing top 50 mm above ground; the raft top here is the modelled ground, so the upstand is not modelled and is recorded.
- Floor on the slab: CMHC Fig. 47 B, sleeper directly on the slab over polyethylene. The floor joists are that sleeper; the polyethylene is named, not modelled.

- Stud height 11.5 m: CMHC Table 25 stops at 4.2 m. The studs carry a light roof only, are restrained in the weak direction every 0.65 m by the rails on both faces, and in the strong direction by the ties to the ring legs at every rail; the ring trusses, not the studs, take the wind. ### 3.1 The two systems

Two separate timber systems, as in the red building (photo rule 2): a self-supporting boarded box, and an exoskeleton of 11 ring trusses standing 0.08 m outside it. The box carries its own floor, walls and roof to the raft. The trusses carry themselves and brace the box; the box is tied to the truss legs at every rail level. Keeping them separate is what lets the trusses ripple while the inside stays a plain box, and it avoids the collision a shared roof would cause (webs rising from a chord that also carries a deck).

Capacity comes from repetition, never from a bigger section: paired slats face to face for studs and joists (60 x 120), paired slats with webs between them for truss chords (the sandwich of photo rule 2 and Erne). ### 3.5 Lateral system, per direction

- Across the trusses (x): each ring truss is a portal whose corners are trussed (chords continuous around the eave, webs continue), so the 11 rings are 11 moment frames. The box's side walls are tied to the legs at every rail (bolts through the outer boards into the leg's inner chord, named, not modelled). Load path: wind on a side wall -> studs -> rails -> ties -> ring legs -> trussed corners and feet -> raft.
- Along the row (y): the rings are thin planes and need bracing between them. Diagonal braces F 30 x 120 in the gap between the box and the legs, lying flat against the legs' inner faces, in the plane x = +/-(2.198 to 2.228). Per side four X's in four panels: y from -3.25 to 0 and from 0 to 3.25, z from 0.15 to 5.95 and from 6.05 to 11.75; each X is the two diagonals of its panel (corner to corner), so 8 diagonals per side, 16 in all, each about 6.65 m long at 61 degrees to the horizontal (CMHC Fig. 86 and FRIM Fig. 30 both want braces at 45 degrees or steeper; one X across the whole row would sit at 42 degrees, which is why the panels are half the row). Halving joint where the two diagonals of an X cross (three boxes, as in the timber-framing skill); each diagonal spliced once at a leg crossing (4.80 + rest), the splice landing on a leg. Horizontal ties F in the same plane at z = 5.95 to 6.07 and z = 11.75 to 11.87 from y = -3.25 to 3.25 (FRIM Table 1 item E2, horizontal brace tying trussed frames). Every diagonal and tie is nailed to every leg it crosses (named, not modelled). Load path: wind on an end wall -> end wall studs -> box roof deck (boards nailed at every chord act as the diaphragm) and the rails -> side walls -> ties to the legs -> braced planes -> feet -> raft. The braced planes reach the eave, so they serve the whole height.
- The box itself: boards nailed to rails and studs on both faces make each wall a shear panel; the floor is on the raft.

### 3.6 The ring trusses and the ripple rule

Plane thickness 120 mm: chord slats at y_i - 0.060 to -0.030 and +0.030 to +0.060; webs in two planes, rising webs at y_i - 0.030 to 0.000, falling webs at 0.000 to +0.030, so the two webs meeting at a node never share a plane. Chord slats F 30 x 120 with the 120 in the truss plane; webs F 30 x 120 likewise.

Inner outline (chord centreline), the same for every truss: (-2.32, 0) -> (-2.32, z_e) -> (0, z_e + 0.387) -> (2.32, z_e) -> (2.32, 0). The 1:6 gable matches the box roof. Inner chord inner face at 2.26, i.e. 0.082 outside the wall face (2.178), room for the y-braces. The inner chord's underside clears the box deck top by about 0.06 at the eave and the apex when z_h = z_e - 0.37.

Arc length s along the inner outline from the left foot (s = 0) to the right foot (s = 2 z_e + 4.704). Truss depth, centreline to centreline, measured along the outward normal:

    d(s, i) = 0.63 + 0.30 * sin(2 * pi * s / 8.0 + 2 * pi * i / 11)      i = 0..10

so d runs from 0.33 to 0.93 m (mine: Erne's trusses are about a metre deep; 0.33 is the least depth that keeps the webs steeper than 40 degrees at a 0.8 m panel). Wavelength 8.0 m along the outline: about 1.5 waves per leg and a little over half a wave across the top, an arc rather than a crenellation. Phase advance 1/11 of a turn per truss: the crest travels one full wavelength across the row, adjacent trusses differ by at most 0.17 m, and the crests run diagonally across the side elevations as in the Tschumi image.

Nodes: inner nodes at the four corners of the outline plus equal subdivisions of every straight run into panels of at most 0.80 m (legs: 15 panels; each half of the top: 3 panels). Outer vertices at every half-panel position and at both feet: Q(s) = P(s) + n(s) d(s, i), n the outward unit normal of the run the point lies on. The outer chord is the polyline through the outer vertices, one straight sandwich pair per segment, consecutive segments mitred on the bisector plane at their shared vertex; the corners of the outline are therefore chamfered by the outer chord, not mitred. Webs: a Warren zigzag, inner node -> next outer vertex -> next inner node, alternating planes, ends inset so no corner crosses the far face of the chord it lands in. Both chords reach z = 0 at each foot.

Overall size rule (brief): W_out = the larger of the plan extents of the outer structure over slat faces (x: outer chord faces at the deepest point, expected 2 x 3.31 = 6.62; y: end truss faces, 2 x 3.31 = 6.62); H_out = highest slat face of the outer chords; H_out = 2.00 x W_out within 1 percent. The Builder measures both on the generated geometry and tunes z_e (expected 11.90) until the ratio holds; z_h follows as z_e - 0.37. Nothing else moves.

# Brief as understood

Build one small room, a single-variation run. The floor plan is square and the building stands twice as tall as it is wide, the proportion measured on the outside of the finished structure. One entrance, one door. Daylight enters only from high up, either through the roof or through a band of windows just under it; the Designer picks one of the two from the red building photos and records the choice. Every member is a thin timber slat: walls, floor, roof and the outer trusses alike are built up from slats, with no sawn heavy sections, no sheet material and no glass modelled beyond the openings. The three photos of the red timber building in `input/` (01-soane-front, 02-soane-outside, 03-soaneinterior-1) set the construction method, the slat sizes and the overall dimensions. The two other images (Erne_Dachbau_778, Tchumi-02) set only the articulation of the roof and the outer structure: a series of trusses whose outlines undulate from one to the next, so that the outside reads as an expressive, rippling structure while the room inside stays a plain square box. Nothing from the red building is preserved literally; its proportions are dropped where they conflict with the 2:1 rule, and the brief wins over the photos on that point.

## Materials overridden

- The red building photos give construction and dimensions, but the 2:1 height rule of the brief overrides whatever proportion the photos show. Recorded as a deliberate deviation in the rationale.
- The Erne Dachbau and Tschumi images give articulation only. Their dimensions, materials and programme are ignored.

## Ambiguities resolved

- "Twice as tall as it is wide": the overall height of the outer structure, ridge or truss top to ground, is twice the outer plan width. The Designer decides how much of that height is the interior room and how much is roof structure; the room inside should still read as a tall square shaft, not a low box under a tall hat.
- "Light from either the roof or the windows close to the roof": one of the two, not both. The Designer chooses whichever the red building photos support and the truss roof allows, and records the reason.
- "Entirely out of thin timber slats": the trusses are built-up slat trusses (laminated, nailed or bolted slat chords and webs), not solid sawn trusses. Slat sizes come from the photos, checked against the manuals by the Researcher.
- "Undulating trusses": the trusses are a series along the building, each with a curved or folded outline, and the outline changes from truss to truss so that the outer surface ripples. The Designer sets the number of trusses, the amplitude and the rule that governs the change.
- Site: flat ground, no terrain, no context buildings.

Concept approved. Here is what fixes the numbers, before any geometry exists.

**Source to rule to number** (from the Researcher's verdict table; the Researcher ran on Sonnet, about 240k tokens and 78 tool calls):

| Topic | Source | What it fixed |
|---|---|---|
| Floor boards | CMHC Table 22 p.287, FRIM Table 1 A7 | 19 mm minimum at 600 mm; B 24 x 120 on joists at 0.65 m is conservative |
| Roof deck | CMHC Table 35 p.305 | 19 mm minimum at 600 mm; F 30 flat on trusses at 0.65 m is conservative |
| Roof heel and pitch | CMHC Fig. 86 p.125, Table 36 p.306; FRIM Sheet 9 | bottom chord bears on the head plate; 1:6 is the low-slope threshold, covering not modelled |
| Built-up members | CMHC p.94; FRIM Sheet 7 p.56 | nails from each side at most 450 mm apart; splices staggered and plated (named, not modelled) |
| Door opening | CMHC p.109, APA p.15-16 | 1.0 m needs one jack per side; the doubled jacks are for the module, not load |
| Bracing angle | CMHC Fig. 86, FRIM Ch. 6 Fig. 30 | 45 degrees or steeper; the along-row X panels were halved so the braces stand at 61 degrees (the one correction research forced) |
| Truss feet | FRIM Sheet 7 p.56 | steel U-strap, two 12.7 mm bolts, named not modelled |
| Floor on slab | CMHC Fig. 47B p.79 | joists as sleepers on polyethylene, named not modelled |
| Door leaf | one approved external source, marked external | braces run hinge-bottom to latch-top; B 24 and F 30 sit inside the stated ranges |
| Tall studs, thin sections, clerestory band, sandwich truss node | not covered by any manual | recorded as departures with a load-path argument; every member is "plausible, not calculated" |

**Key numbers.** Room 3.90 x 3.90 m clear, floor at 0.144 m. Outer structure 6.62 x 6.62 m in plan and 13.24 m tall, the 2:1 ratio held by a script assertion while the Builder tunes one eave height. Two sections only, F 30 x 120 for framing and B 24 x 120 for boards. Eleven ring trusses at 0.65 m centres, each a closed ring with a 1:6 gabled top, 120 mm thick with paired chords sandwiching single webs. Depth ripples between 0.33 and 0.93 m by a sine along the outline (8 m wavelength) whose phase advances a tenth of a turn per truss, so the crests run diagonally across the sides as in the Tschumi image. Light band from 9.63 m to the wall head, about 1.9 m tall, bare mullions, on all four sides. Door 1.00 x 2.10 m in the south wall.

**Deliberate deviations from the photos.** Undercroft on heavy posts and the external stair dropped. The red building's 1.5:1 box becomes a 2:1 outer structure with a 2.9:1 room. The scaffold with walkways and corrugated band becomes the ring trusses and an open band. The squat hatch becomes a full door. Frame bays go from 1.1 m to the 0.65 m module. The arched corrugated roof becomes a 1:6 board gable with no covering. Erne's laminated curves become mitred 0.8 m straight segments. Red paint not modelled.

# Design notes, experiment 16, Fable run

Decisions in the order I made them, with the alternatives that lost. Applies to v01 unless a later entry says otherwise. Dated 2026-09-14.

## Concept stage

**Roles of the images.** The three red-building photos give construction and proportion (photo rules 1 to 8 in concept.md); Erne gives the truss type, Tschumi the surface behaviour (rules 9, 10). I measured nothing on the last two.

**Calibration.** The only object of known size in photo 01 is the external stair: 14 risers, about 2.4 m, over 255 px, so about 105 px/m. I cross-checked with the board count on the far wall in photo 03 (31 boards at 130 to 140 mm, a 4.1 to 4.3 m room). The door was no use for calibration: it reads as a squat hatch about 0.8 m wide and 0.75 m tall, so either the room is 4 m wide and the door is tiny, or the door is normal and the room is 8 m wide and 17 m tall. The board count settles it for the small room; I read the door as a deliberate oddity of the original and replaced it (see below).

**Light: the band, not the roof.** Photo 01 shows a translucent corrugated band 1.8 m tall under an opaque roof; photo 03 shows the white band at the top of the side walls and a dark deck. Both photos say band. A rooflight would also sit under the ring trusses' top chords and be shaded by them. The band is open framing, no glass, per the brief. Rejected: a rooflight (unsupported by the photos, shaded by the trusses); band plus rooflight (brief says one of the two).

**Undercroft dropped.** The red building stands on a 2.4 m undercroft of heavy sawn posts with an external stair. The brief forbids heavy sections, puts the building on flat ground and wants one entrance. So the room stands on a raft flush with the ground, floor 0.144 above it. Rejected: a slat-framed undercroft (adds a storey the brief did not ask for and turns the one entrance into a stair).

**Two systems, not one.** The box carries itself; the ring trusses stand 0.08 m outside it and brace it. I tried the alternative first, the trusses carrying the box roof on their inner top chords, and it fails geometrically: the webs rise from the inner chord through any deck laid on it, in every sandwich arrangement I drew (webs between the chord slats, webs on the chord faces, purlins between nodes). Only a deck hung under the inner chord avoids the collision, and then the "roof" is a ceiling with no bearing for a covering. The red building has the same two-system logic (photo rule 2), so the separation is also the more faithful reading. Consequence: the box has its own slat roof trusses, which photo 03 shows anyway.

**Module 0.65 m and 11 trusses.** The plan is square inside (brief) and the outer structure should be square too, otherwise "twice as tall as wide" has two answers. Ring trusses wrap the box in one direction only (Erne, one direction), so the row's length in y has to match the trusses' width in x, about 6.6 m. Ten bays of 0.65 give 6.5 m between end planes, and 6 x 0.65 = 3.90 gives the room, so studs, floor joists, roof trusses and ring trusses share one module and one origin. Rejected: 0.60 module with 11 trusses (row 6.1 m, not square); 0.60 module with 12 trusses (no truss at y = 0, room 4.2, outer 6.9 x 6.7, height 13.8); 9 trusses at 0.80 (the ripple reads as steps, adjacent trusses differ by up to 0.2 m over 0.8 m).

**Ripple rule.** d(s, i) = 0.63 + 0.30 sin(2 pi s / 8.0 + 2 pi i / 11), s the arc length along the inner outline, i the truss index. Depth 0.33 to 0.93 m: the minimum keeps webs steeper than 40 degrees on a 0.8 m panel, the maximum is what fits a 6.62 m outer width. Wavelength 8.0 m: 1.5 waves per leg, half a wave over the top, an arc like Erne's rather than a serration. Phase 1/11 turn per truss: adjacent trusses differ by at most 0.17 m, and the crest line crosses the side elevation diagonally, which is the Tschumi effect. Rejected: a ripple in the inner chord too (the inner chord is what the box ties to and what stands on the shoe; it should be straight); a wave symmetric about the apex (kills the diagonal travel); amplitude 0.20 (a 0.4 m ripple on a 6.6 m elevation is 6 percent, hard to see).

**Inner outline as a 1:6 gable.** The ring's inner top chord follows the box roof at 0.07 clear, so the box roof and the ring have the same pitch. A flat inner chord would need a flat box roof with no fall. 1:6 is below the 1:3 threshold where ceiling ties stop being required, but the box roof trusses tie their heels anyway.

**Truss plane 120 mm thick, webs in two planes.** With one web plane (chord + 30 gap + chord) the two webs meeting at a node collide. A 60 mm gap gives the rising webs and the falling webs their own 30 mm plane, each nailed to the chord slat on its side. Rejected: gusseted nodes (no sheet material); lapping the webs (an extra joint type per node).

**Y-bracing in the gap.** The braces between ring legs cannot lie on the outer chord (it ripples) or inside the truss depth (webs). They lie flat on the legs' inner faces, in the 0.082 m gap between the box and the legs, as two X's per side with halving joints at the crossings and horizontal ties at the X ends. The red building's red diagonals sit in the same place relative to its box. Rejected: single tension diagonals per side (a compression diagonal 8.7 m long in a slat buckles, and the two sides would have to share load through the box); braces inside the truss depth (collide with webs).

**Door 1.00 x 2.10 with doubled jacks.** The module gives 1.12 clear between single jacks on the +/-0.65 kings; doubled jacks bring it to 1.00. Opening size follows the door, not the grid. Header of four slats on edge (120 x 120) for a 1.0 m span under a light roof. Rejected: the photo's squat 0.8 x 0.75 hatch (not a door); a header of paired slats only (60 wide, would not fill the stud zone and the cripples would land on nothing).

**Raft.** One concrete element, 7.20 x 7.20 x 0.25, top at the ground. It is the modelled ground, not a timber member. Rejected: pads under each truss foot plus a slab under the box (22 pads plus a slab, more elements for the same statement); no foundation (truss feet on nothing).

**Piece count.** About 3200 pieces, 1780 of them in the ring trusses. If the check loop cannot carry it, the panel length goes from 0.80 to 1.00 first; the truss count and module stay. Reported to CraftBot.

## Research round (v01)

**What the manuals settled.** Board spans (CMHC Tables 22 and 35, FRIM A7): both boards are conservative at 0.65 m. Heel bearing over the wall plate (CMHC Fig. 86). 1:6 is CMHC's low-slope threshold, so the box roof would need a membrane; not modelled by the brief's rule against sheet material. A 1.0 m door needs one jack per side; my doubled jacks are for the opening size, kept. Post base as a steel U-strap with two bolts (FRIM Sheet 7), named. Sleeper on slab over polyethylene (CMHC Fig. 47 B), named.

**What the manuals corrected.** Brace angle: CMHC and FRIM both want 45 degrees or steeper; my two X's per side across the whole 6.5 m row stood at 42 degrees. Changed to four X's per side in 3.25 m wide panels, 61 degrees, 16 diagonals in all. Rejected: three X's over the height across the full row (steeper is taller and narrower, so more panels over the height make it worse, 31 degrees); a single K per panel (a compression diagonal in a 30 mm slat over 6 m).

**What the manuals do not reach, and what I did instead.** No manual states 30 x 120 or 24 x 120 as structural members (FRIM's thinnest are 35 x 72 truss members); no stud table goes past 4.2 m (CMHC Table 25) against my 11.5 m; CMHC's minimum column is 140 x 140. The brief asks for thin slats, so these are departures by instruction, and the compensating devices are the ones in the concept: pairing, rails every 0.65 m on both faces, ties to the ring legs at every rail, and the trusses rather than the studs taking the wind. TRADA's 600 mm batten maximum against my 0.65 m rails: 50 mm over, kept for the one-module argument. The sandwich truss node and the clerestory band are extensions by analogy and are labelled so in concept 4. All of it goes into the rationale's deviation ledger under "outside the manuals".

**External search.** Approved one: a ledged-and-braced board door, because no manual names it. The leaf is a small element; the sizes in the concept are mine until the row lands and stay mine if the source disagrees only in millimetres.


## v01 Builder questions (2026-09-14, applies to v02 and later)

The v01 Builder found five places where a concept number contradicted the concept's own geometry and resolved each toward the checkable requirement, plus three open questions. My answers, with what lost. Concept numbers patched in place (sections 1, 3.2, 3.3.5, 3.3.6, 3.3.8, 3.5, 3.6), each patch marked "v01 derived constant" or "v02".

**1. Box roof end trusses at y = +/-1.89, confirmed.** The end wall's inner rail starts at 1.974 and its stud zone at 2.004; a 120 mm truss centred on 1.95 reaches 2.01 and cuts both. At 1.89 the outer slat face sits on the inner board plane. The truss still bears on the side wall head plate, which spreads the 60 mm offset from the stud pair at 1.95; the vertical-alignment rule is about load reaching a stud line, and a 60 mm eccentricity on a 120 mm plate over a 60 mm stud pair is within the plate. Lost: five trusses with the gable plate carrying the deck edge (deck span 0.76 at the ends breaks R-24's 0.65); moving the end walls out (changes the room, R-01).

**2. Deck eave at x = 2.249 and top chord tails at 2.22, confirmed.** My 2.28 was an arithmetic slip against my own leg inner face at 2.26. Nineteen whole 120 boards along a 1:6 slope give 2.249 in plan, no ripped board, 0.071 overhang past the wall face. The chord tails at 2.22 stay under the deck and clear the brace plane. Lost: legs moved out to 2.35 (changes W_out, every leg and the 2:1 tuning, for a 30 mm overhang).

**3. Brace plane at x = 2.230 to 2.260, confirmed.** The concept's sentence was right ("flat against the legs' inner faces") and its numbers wrong. The braces work only if they are nailed to every leg they cross, so contact is the rule and 2.198 to 2.228 was a typo. Clear of the wall face by 0.052; the box-to-leg ties are still named, not modelled.

**4. Upper tie at deck underside minus 10 mm (11.669 to 11.789), lower panel top at 6.07, confirmed.** The tie's job is to hold the top of the braced panel at the eave and tie the legs together there; 10 mm under the deck edge is as high as it gets without cutting the deck or the ring's corner mitre. Written as a rule, not a number, because z_h is tuned by the Builder. The 6.05 was another slip (20 mm overlap with the lower tie's top at 6.07). Lost: the deck pulled back to 2.22 to keep the tie at 11.75 (the deck would then overhang the wall by 42 mm and the tie would sit above the head plate for no reason).

**5. Splices, confirmed with one change.** The rule is now a number: splices on a rail centre (sill rail included) or a truss node, the two slats of a pair at least one module apart on studs and two panels apart on chords; "half a length" is gone. Side wall studs (A 4.55/9.10, B 2.60/7.15, stagger 1.95) and leg chords (A nodes 6/12, B nodes 4/10, stagger two panels) pass. The gable studs' third cut at the sill rail does not: it put the B splice at 9.57, 0.47 from the A splice at 9.10. B at 3.25/7.80 instead gives pieces 3.25, 4.55 and at most 4.37 m to the apex (deck underside 11.85 to 12.17), two splices per slat, stagger 1.30 from A, all on rails. Same set for the door cripples. Lost: the third cut (more pieces, less stagger); a B set at 3.90/8.45 (stagger 0.65, the minimum, when 1.30 is free).

**6. Outer chord corners mitred, confirmed; the depth floor stays at 0.33.** The offset-polygon vertex is the honest geometry of an offset polyline; the chamfer was a shortcut in my node rule that the wave exposed at eight of 22 eave corners. Raising the minimum depth to 0.50 (d = 0.75 +/- 0.25) would push the maximum to 1.00, W_out to about 6.76 and every tuned number with it, and would still leave a chamfered shoulder at the eave where the ring should read as a gable on legs. Structurally the corner vertex is a kink in the outer chord with no web to it, about 0.4 m from the adjacent outer vertices each way; the chord is a nailed sandwich pair and the kink is a mitre in both slats, so the deviation force at the kink goes into the two webs either side. Recorded as an unbraced kink, plausible at this scale, not calculated. Lost: a web to the corner vertex (no free web plane at a corner node).

**7. R-28 covers the y-bracing only.** CMHC Fig. 86 and FRIM Fig. 30 are about braces that stiffen a frame or a wall. The leaf braces stop a 1.0 x 2.1 board door from sagging on its hinges; their angle follows from three ledges at 0.80 spacing on a 1.00 leaf, and ledged-and-braced doors run at 30 to 40 degrees as a type (the external row). Ledge spacing unchanged. Lost: two ledges at 1.60 spacing to steepen the braces (the boards would span 1.6 m between fixings, and the leaf is not a wall).

**8. Eave slot open, part of the band (new R-34).** Photo rule 4 has the translucent band directly under the opaque roof, and inside a white band under a dark deck with the slat trusses standing in it (rule 5). That is what the open slot gives: the band runs from the sill rail at 9.63 to the deck underside, the head plate and head rails are a transom across it, and the roof truss heels stand in the band as in photo 03. A board strip between the heels would put a dark fascia between the band and the roof, which neither photo shows. Structurally nothing changes: the deck diaphragm reaches the side wall through the truss heels on the head plate, not through any board in the slot. R-05 reworded so the slot is not "another opening". Lost: a 0.24 board fascia between heels (unlike the photos, about 60 pieces for nothing the load path needs).

**Not asked, accepted as read.** Derived constants 6 to 8 of the v01 notes: the end walls drop the +/-1.95 module stud where it overlaps the end stud (R-15 reworded); the door leaf's hinge stile against the jamb lining at -2.004 so the open leaf touches the wall; the bottom plate and outer bottom rail continuous under the door as the one threshold step. The four-slat corner post above the side head plate and the 30 x 30 notch in the outer rail at each eave corner are Builder detailing inside the concept and need no line.

## Phase 2, structural review (2026-09-14, on v03, reference set aside)

Read from `version_notes.md` v01 to v03 and `inspection_v03.md`, not from the concept. The checklist of the structural-logic skill, item by item.

**1. Vertical load paths, as sentences.** Ring trusses: outer and inner chord pairs of every ring end on the raft at z = 0 at both feet (steel U-strap and two bolts named, FRIM Sheet 7, not modelled); webs between the chord slats carry the truss's own weight down both chords. Box roof: deck boards on the top chords of 7 sandwich trusses at 0.65 (end pair at +/-1.89), bottom chords on the side wall head plates over the full stud zone, head plates on paired studs at 0.65 (spliced one slat at a time on rail centres, partner continuous), studs on the bottom plate on the raft; the gable head plates carry the deck edge straight into the end wall studs. Door: header of four slats on doubled jacks on the plate. Floor: boards on joists lying on the raft. Braces and ties: nailed to the legs they cross. Every family closes to the raft; nothing floats (0 floating in v03).

**2. Lateral, per direction.** Across the trusses (x): 11 rings with trussed corners (the mitred outer vertex at each eave and the webs from the corner node to both neighbouring outer vertices make the corner a truss, so "portal" is earned, not assumed); the box is tied to the legs at rail levels (named). Each ring takes its own 0.65 m strip; no diaphragm needed. Along the row (y): the two braced planes at x = +/-2.245 (four X's per side at 59 to 61 degrees, ties at 6.0 and 11.6) from z 0.15 to 11.7; the box deck brings the end walls' wind to the side walls through the truss heels on the head plates, and the rails and ties bring it to the legs. The braced planes reach the eave. Above the upper tie the 11 ring tops (4.7 m arches, 1.4 m above the tie) are tied to nothing in y: each top run stands as a cantilever from its own braced legs. Finding, see 6.

**3. Bearing at seats, continuity.** Bottom chords on head plates for 0.12 (the stud zone); top chords seated on the bottom chord's arris at the heel; deck on chord tops across every truss; joists flat on the raft; truss feet square on the raft; header on jacks 0.12 each side; bottom plate and outer bottom rail continuous under the door (the threshold). Ring chord splices on nodes, two panels apart in a pair; stud splices on rail centres one module apart. Discontinuities walked: door (header, cripples), eave slot (the deck reaches the side wall only through the seven heels, a named nailed connection, fine for a diaphragm on a 4.3 m span), gable corners (four-slat corner post from the side head plate to the gable plate).

**4. Foundations.** The raft is the modelled ground; undersides irrelevant on flat ground. FRIM's 50 mm footing upstand under each truss foot and the polyethylene under the joists are not modelled (no terrain, no moisture in the vocabulary). Overturning of a 13.2 m tall, 6.6 m wide frame is held by the named hold-downs at 44 feet and a 31 t raft; not calculated, recorded.

**5. Sizes and restraint, the one real finding.** The sections are outside every manual and are recorded (R-32). What the model does not yet do is give the ring chords a weak-axis restraint. The inner leg chords are crossed by the braces and ties every 2.5 to 3 m, which is a restraint. The outer chords, 28 m of paired 30 mm slats per ring, are restrained out of their plane by nothing at all between the raft and the raft: the top run's outer chord is a compression chord under its own weight and under wind on the row, the leg's outer chord is in compression under wind from the far side, and a 30 x 120 slat pair with a 28 m unbraced length is a mechanism, not a member. The inner top chords over the roof are in the same state (no tie in y except through the legs). In a built Erne roof the purlins and the roof plane do this job; here the ripple forbids a straight purlin, but short spacers between adjacent trusses do not need to be straight across the row. Action: requirement P2-01, spacers F 30 x 120 between the chord faces of adjacent rings, at every third outer vertex along the outer chord (about every 2.4 m along the outline; each spacer runs between the two outer vertices at the same s, so it is inclined by the depth difference, at most 0.17 over 0.53) and at every inner node of the top runs (six per bay), nailed to both chord faces. About 120 outer and 60 inner pieces. Rejected: straight purlins over the outer chords (cannot lie on a rippling surface); nothing (the weak-axis length stays 28 m; the review exists to catch exactly this).

**6. Lateral in y above the tie.** With the spacers the 11 tops become a grid, and a grid without diagonals holds only by chord bending. Action: P2-02, one zigzag of diagonals per slope in the roof plane, F 30 x 120 laid flat in the 0.07 gap under the inner top chords (top face on the chord undersides, 0.04 clear of the deck), from the eave line to the apex line over three bays each (plan angle about 50 degrees; FRIM Sheet 9 puts its roof diagonal at 45), from truss 0 to truss 9 and its mirror so they form X's; bay 9 to 10 stays unbraced, the end truss being held by the spacers. 16 pieces of about 3.05 m. Rejected: diagonals on top of the outer chords (the ripple); diagonals under the deck inside the box (R-08, the inside stays plain).

**7. Details by gravity, sliding, moisture, racking.** Posts on the slab: shoes named, upstand not modelled. Roof drains at 1:6 to both eaves over the open eave slot and past the 0.08 gap; no gutter in the vocabulary, recorded. Halving joints thin each brace to 15 mm at the crossing; standard for slat X-bracing, kept. Racking of the box: two board faces on rails; kept.

**Considered and not changed.** The box roof trusses' 0.12 heel depth for a 4.25 m span (apex depth about 0.5, span/9, plausible for a light deck); the 0.24 m open eave slot (the diaphragm goes through the heels, not through boards); the porch bays' free trusses (braced by the same planes as the rest); the 60 x 120 studs at 11.3 m (restrained every 0.65 on both faces, and the wind is the rings' job, not theirs).

Closing line: every section is plausible for its span, none is calculated.

## Phase 2, comparison round (2026-09-14, v03 against the references)

One Inspector on views 10 (matched to photo 01), 01 to 04, 06, 13, 16, 18, 21; its table is `inspection_v03_comparison.md`. My verdicts, one row per difference it raised. Nothing here spends a version.

| In the reference | In the model | Change or kept, with reason |
|---|---|---|
| Door leaf: ledged-and-braced boards (rule 7) | View 18 shows the leaf as a blown-out white slab, no boards, ledges or braces legible | Kept. The v02 Inspector read the leaf on view 26 (vertical boards, three ledges, two braces low at the hinge side, high at the latch side) and the leaf has not changed since; view 18 looks through the open door into the light and over-exposes the leaf. Not geometry. If a later version re-renders, add view 26 to the set. |
| Horizontal dado joint about 1 m up (rule 6) | Board joints at 1.95 (B columns) and 3.25 (A columns), none near 1 m | Kept. The photo's joint at 1 m is the head rail of its 0.75 m hatch; with a 2.10 door the corresponding line is the header at 2.24, and the B joint at 1.95 sits near it. A third joint at 1 m would break every board into a piece under 1 m for no structural reason. |
| Light band 1.8 m (rule 4) | About 2.2 m (9.63 to the head at 11.48, and the open eave slot above it) | Kept. Scaled with the shaft (photo band is 0.3 of its 6.1 m room; ours is 0.19 of 11.3 m, already the smaller reading). Below 1.8 m the band stops reading as a band from the ground. |
| Erne webs at 50 to 65 degrees (rule 9) | 40 to 67 degrees across the ripple | Kept. The 0.8 m panel at the shallowest depth 0.33 gives 40 degrees; the alternative, a minimum depth of 0.5, halves the ripple's amplitude. Argued in concept 3.6. |
| Dark opaque deck against a light band (rule 4/5) | Deck opaque and closed, but the same tone as the walls | Kept, out of vocabulary. Colour is not geometry; the viewer's layer colours can darken the deck. |
| Few bold paired posts (rule 2) | A fine Warren lattice on every leg | Kept. The lattice is the Erne truss the brief asked for; the photo's scaffold posts were replaced by decision (deviation table row 3). |
| Undercroft and stair (rule 8) | Building on the raft | Kept, recorded deviation (brief). |
| Curved chords (rule 9) | Straight 0.8 m mitred segments | Kept, recorded deviation (vocabulary). |
| Ripple on a true side elevation (rule 10) | Not judged (view 07 not in the subset) | The v01 Builder already found that an orthographic side elevation cannot show a depth that varies toward the camera; view 21 was added for that reason and the Inspector read the diagonal crests on it. No action. |

Matched view 10 against photo 01: the silhouette's proportion is close; what differs is what fills it (many thin members instead of a few bold ones, no undercroft, low colour contrast), and all three are decided deviations. Requirement line P2-04 records the round as kept.
=====
# Version notes, experiment 16, Fable run

One entry per version. The next Builder starts from the last entry.

## v01 (2026-09-14)

Script `experiment_16_fable_v01.py`, views `views_fable.py` (views 01 to 20 rendered, 21 appended for v02). First version, from the template. Everything in concept.md sections 3.3 to 3.6 is built: raft, floor, four layered walls with the door, box roof with deck, 11 ring trusses, y-bracing.

Numbers: 3248 members (3247 timber pieces plus the raft; ring trusses 1782, box 1393, bracing 72). 32 penetrating pairs, 0 floating. Render-and-check pass 37 s wall clock for 20 views, so the truss panel fallback (0.80 to 1.00 m) was not needed and was not applied.

2:1 rule, measured on the generated geometry (R-02): z_e = 11.9481 (bisection, 60 steps, on the outer-face polyline of all 11 trusses), z_h = 11.5781. W_out = 6.6206 (x extent 6.621, y extent 6.620), H_out = 13.2417, H/W = 2.0001. Asserted in the script within 0.01, plan square within 0.05 (R-03). Leg panels 15 of 0.7965 m, top halves 3 of 0.784 m.

### Pair families

Two rows in the table, one cause. All 32 pairs are RingIn x RingOut at 30 mm (28) or 28 mm (4), on trusses 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, four pairs each: the chamfer segment of the outer chord that skips an eave corner (segment 21 at the +x corner, segment 15 at the -x corner) passes through the inner chord's corner (both slats of the leg's top piece and of the top run). The concept's rule puts outer vertices only at half-panel points and at the feet, so the outer chord cuts across each corner between the vertex 0.40 below it on the leg and the vertex 0.39 along the top. The distance from that chamfer line to the corner is about 0.74 (d - 0.325): at d = 0.63 it is 0.225 and clears; at d = 0.33 it is 0.004, straight through the corner. Anything under d = 0.49 collides, and the wave puts eight of the 22 eave corners there.

Fix for v02 (one function, `ring_nodes`): add an outer vertex at each of the three outline corners, on the corner bisector at the offset-polygon position P_c + (n1 + n2) d(s_c, i) / (1 + n1 . n2). The depth rule stays as written (d measured along the normal of both runs at the corner); the outer chord gets a mitred kink at the corner instead of the chamfer. No web to the corner vertex: the 60 gap holds two web planes, and both are taken at a corner node by the rising and falling webs. The panel-to-vertex index shift (outer[j + 1]) must then be replaced by a stored mid-vertex index per panel. The concept sentence "the corners of the outline are therefore chamfered by the outer chord, not mitred" changes; Designer question 6 below.

### Derived constants that depart from the concept's numbers

Each of these is a contradiction inside the concept resolved toward the checkable requirement; none narrows the brief. Numbered as Designer questions at the end.

1. Box roof end trusses at y = +/-1.89, not +/-1.95. A truss centred on 1.95 has slats to 2.01, 60 mm inside the end wall (inner board face 1.950, stud zone from 2.004): it would cut the end wall's inner head rail and the gable studs. At 1.89 the outer slat face is flush with the inner board face; deck spans 0.59 and 0.17 m at the ends (R-24 holds).
2. Deck eave at x = 2.249 (19 whole 120 boards from the eave to the apex), not 2.28. The ring legs' inner face is at 2.26; a deck to 2.28 runs 20 mm into every leg the deck crosses. Overhang past the wall face 0.071 instead of 0.10. Top chord tails end at 2.22 (0.096 past the head plate, R-25's 0.11 holds) so they clear the brace plane.
3. Braces and ties in x = 2.230 to 2.260, not 2.198 to 2.228. The concept says "flat against the legs' inner faces" and R-20 wants contact with every leg; 2.228 leaves 32 mm to the leg face at 2.26. Clear of the wall face by 0.052.
4. Upper tie at z 11.669 to 11.789 (derived: deck underside at the eave minus 10 mm), not 11.75 to 11.87, which would cut through the deck eave (z 11.79 to 11.83 at x 2.23 to 2.25) and the ring's corner mitre. Upper brace panel z 6.07 to 11.669 (the concept's 6.05 overlaps the lower tie's top at 6.07 by 20 mm). Angles 59.9 to 60.7 degrees, asserted at or above 45.
5. Splices. Slats over 4.80 m are split at supports, A and B slats of a pair staggered: side wall studs at rail centres 4.55 and 9.10 (A) and 2.60 and 7.15 (B), gable studs get a third cut at the sill rail (9.57) where the last piece would exceed 4.80; ring inner leg chords at nodes 6 and 12 (A) and 4 and 10 (B); braces spliced on the leg at y = -1.30 or 1.30; ties at y = 1.30. Splice sets (3, 9) for the leg B slat failed the length assertion at 4.83 because the corner mitre adds 50 mm to the top piece. Longest piece in the model 4.788 m (asserted at 4.80 plus 20 mm for bevelled ends).
6. End walls drop the +/-1.95 module stud: it would overlap the end stud at 1.944 to 2.004. End studs at +/-1.974 stand in for it.
7. Door leaf hinge stile at y = -2.004 (against the jamb lining) so the open leaf touches the wall and the contact check sees it; concept placed the leaf from -1.950.
8. Bottom plate and outer bottom rail run continuous under the door: the sill is 0.144 above the raft, so they form the single step of the threshold. The inner bottom rail stops at the opening.

### What the renders show (Builder's look at 01, 07, 11, 13; no Inspector, over the threshold)

The ripple reads in the orbits. View 07, the side elevation from +x, does not show it at all: the depth varies toward the camera, and orthographic projection flattens it. View 21 (azim 12, elev 10) is appended for v02. The end elevation (06) shows the wave as the superimposed outlines of the 11 trusses. The node close-up (11) shows web ends flush inside the sandwich, the chord splices, and the brace halving joints. The section (13) shows the shaft, the band and the box roof trusses; there is a small dark artefact at the ring apex above the inner chord that the v02 Inspector should check on view 19 (apex webs or the top-run mitre).

Not yet judged (Inspector items for v02): closure of the eaves. Between the side wall head plate (z_h) and the deck underside (z_h + 0.24) the side walls are open between the roof truss heels, 0.24 m tall, for the full length. The concept says nothing about it; a board strip between heels would close it. Also the corner block above the side head plate at each e

1	# Design notes, experiment 16, Fable run
2	
3	Decisions in the order I made them, with the alternatives that lost. Applies to v01 unless a later entry says otherwise. Dated 2026-09-14.
4	
5	## Concept stage
6	
7	**Roles of the images.** The three red-building photos give construction and proportion (photo rules 1 to 8 in concept.md); Erne gives the truss type, Tschumi the surface behaviour (rules 9, 10). I measured nothing on the last two.
8	
9	**Calibration.** The only object of known size in photo 01 is the external stair: 14 risers, about 2.4 m, over 255 px, so about 105 px/m. I cross-checked with the board count on the far wall in photo 03 (31 boards at 130 to 140 mm, a 4.1 to 4.3 m room). The door was no use for calibration: it reads as a squat hatch about 0.8 m wide and 0.75 m tall, so either the room is 4 m wide and the door is tiny, or the door is normal and the room is 8 m wide and 17 m tall. The board count settles it for the small room; I read the door as a deliberate oddity of the original and replaced it (see below).
10	
11	**Light: the band, not the roof.** Photo 01 shows a translucent corrugated band 1.8 m tall under an opaque roof; photo 03 shows the white band at the top of the side walls and a dark deck. Both photos say band. A rooflight would also sit under the ring trusses' top chords and be shaded by them. The band is open framing, no glass, per the brief. Rejected: a rooflight (unsupported by the photos, shaded by the trusses); band plus rooflight (brief says one of the two).
12	
13	**Undercroft dropped.** The red building stands on a 2.4 m undercroft of heavy sawn posts with an external stair. The brief forbids heavy sections, puts the building on flat ground and wants one entrance. So the room stands on a raft flush with the ground, floor 0.144 above it. Rejected: a slat-framed undercroft (adds a storey the brief did not ask for and turns the one entrance into a stair).
14	
15	**Two systems, not one.** The box carries itself; the ring trusses stand 0.08 m outside it and brace it. I tried the alternative first, the trusses carrying the box roof on their inner top chords, and it fails geometrically: the webs rise from the inner chord through any deck laid on it, in every sandwich arrangement I drew (webs between the chord slats, webs on the chord faces, purlins between nodes). Only a deck hung under the inner chord avoids the collision, and then the "roof" is a ceiling with no bearing for a covering. The red building has the same two-system logic (photo rule 2), so the separation is also the more faithful reading. Consequence: the box has its own slat roof trusses, which photo 03 shows anyway.
16	
17	**Module 0.65 m and 11 trusses.** The plan is square inside (brief) and the outer structure should be square too, otherwise "twice as tall as wide" has two answers. Ring trusses wrap the box in one direction only (Erne, one direction), so the row's length in y has to match the trusses' width in x, about 6.6 m. Ten bays of 0.65 give 6.5 m between end planes, and 6 x 0.65 = 3.90 gives the room, so studs, floor joists, roof trusses and ring trusses share one module and one origin. Rejected: 0.60 module with 11 trusses (row 6.1 m, not square); 0.60 module with 12 trusses (no truss at y = 0, room 4.2, outer 6.9 x 6.7, height 13.8); 9 trusses at 0.80 (the ripple reads as steps, adjacent trusses differ by up to 0.2 m over 0.8 m).
18	
19	**Ripple rule.** d(s, i) = 0.63 + 0.30 sin(2 pi s / 8.0 + 2 pi i / 11), s the arc length along the inner outline, i the truss index. Depth 0.33 to 0.93 m: the minimum keeps webs steeper than 40 degrees on a 0.8 m panel, the maximum is what fits a 6.62 m outer width. Wavelength 8.0 m: 1.5 waves per leg, half a wave over the top, an arc like Erne's rather than a serration. Phase 1/11 turn per truss: adjacent trusses differ by at most 0.17 m, and the crest line crosses the side elevation diagonally, which is the Tschumi effect. Rejected: a ripple in the inner chord too (the inner chord is what the box ties to and what stands on the shoe; it should be straight); a wave symmetric about the apex (kills the diagonal travel); amplitude 0.20 (a 0.4 m ripple on a 6.6 m elevation is 6 percent, hard to see).
20	
21	**Inner outline as a 1:6 gable.** The ring's inner top chord follows the box roof at 0.07 clear, so the box roof and the ring have the same pitch. A flat inner chord would need a flat box roof with no fall. 1:6 is below the 1:3 threshold where ceiling ties stop being required, but the box roof trusses tie their heels anyway.
22	
23	**Truss plane 120 mm thick, webs in two planes.** With one web plane (chord + 30 gap + chord) the two webs meeting at a node collide. A 60 mm gap gives the rising webs and the falling webs their own 30 mm plane, each nailed to the chord slat on its side. Rejected: gusseted nodes (no sheet material); lapping the webs (an extra joint type per node).
24	
25	**Y-bracing in the gap.** The braces between ring legs cannot lie on the outer chord (it ripples) or inside the truss depth (webs). They lie flat on the legs' inner faces, in the 0.082 m gap between the box and the legs, as two X's per side with halving joints at the crossings and horizontal ties at the X ends. The red building's red diagonals sit in the same place relative to its box. Rejected: single tension diagonals per side (a compression diagonal 8.7 m long in a slat buckles, and the two sides would have to share load through the box); braces inside the truss depth (collide with webs).
26	
27	**Door 1.00 x 2.10 with doubled jacks.** The module gives 1.12 clear between single jacks on the +/-0.65 kings; doubled jacks bring it to 1.00. Opening size follows the door, not the grid. Header of four slats on edge (120 x 120) for a 1.0 m span under a light roof. Rejected: the photo's squat 0.8 x 0.75 hatch (not a door); a header of paired slats only (60 wide, would not fill the stud zone and the cripples would land on nothing).
28

# Design notes, experiment 16, Fable run

Decisions in the order I made them, with the alternatives that lost. Applies to v01 unless a later entry says otherwise. Dated 2026-09-14.

## Concept stage

**Roles of the images.** The three red-building photos give construction and proportion (photo rules 1 to 8 in concept.md); Erne gives the truss type, Tschumi the surface behaviour (rules 9, 10). I measured nothing on the last two.

**Calibration.** The only object of known size in photo 01 is the external stair: 14 risers, about 2.4 m, over 255 px, so about 105 px/m. I cross-checked with the board count on the far wall in photo 03 (31 boards at 130 to 140 mm, a 4.1 to 4.3 m room). The door was no use for calibration: it reads as a squat hatch about 0.8 m wide and 0.75 m tall, so either the room is 4 m wide and the door is tiny, or the door is normal and the room is 8 m wide and 17 m tall. The board count settles it for the small room; I read the door as a deliberate oddity of the original and replaced it (see below).

**Light: the band, not the roof.** Photo 01 shows a translucent corrugated band 1.8 m tall under an opaque roof; photo 03 shows the white band at the top of the side walls and a dark deck. Both photos say band. A rooflight would also sit under the ring trusses' top chords and be shaded by them. The band is open framing, no glass, per the brief. Rejected: a rooflight (unsupported by the photos, shaded by the trusses); band plus rooflight (brief says one of the two).

**Undercroft dropped.** The red building stands on a 2.4 m undercroft of heavy sawn posts with an external stair. The brief forbids heavy sections, puts the building on flat ground and wants one entrance. So the room stands on a raft flush with the ground, floor 0.144 above it. Rejected: a slat-framed undercroft (adds a storey the brief did not ask for and turns the one entrance into a stair).

**Two systems, not one.** The box carries itself; the ring trusses stand 0.08 m outside it and brace it. I tried the alternative first, the trusses carrying the box roof on their inner top chords, and it fails geometrically: the webs rise from the inner chord through any deck laid on it, in every sandwich arrangement I drew (webs between the chord slats, webs on the chord faces, purlins between nodes). Only a deck hung under the inner chord avoids the collision, and then the "roof" is a ceiling with no bearing for a covering. The red building has the same two-system logic (photo rule 2), so the separation is also the more faithful reading. Consequence: the box has its own slat roof trusses, which photo 03 shows anyway.

**Module 0.65 m and 11 trusses.** The plan is square inside (brief) and the outer structure should be square too, otherwise "twice as tall as wide" has two answers. Ring trusses wrap the box in one direction only (Erne, one direction), so the row's length in y has to match the trusses' width in x, about 6.6 m. Ten bays of 0.65 give 6.5 m between end planes, and 6 x 0.65 = 3.90 gives the room, so studs, floor joists, roof trusses and ring trusses share one module and one origin. Rejected: 0.60 module with 11 trusses (row 6.1 m, not square); 0.60 module with 12 trusses (no truss at y = 0, room 4.2, outer 6.9 x 6.7, height 13.8); 9 trusses at 0.80 (the ripple reads as steps, adjacent trusses differ by up to 0.2 m over 0.8 m).

**Ripple rule.** d(s, i) = 0.63 + 0.30 sin(2 pi s / 8.0 + 2 pi i / 11), s the arc length along the inner outline, i the truss index. Depth 0.33 to 0.93 m: the minimum keeps webs steeper than 40 degrees on a 0.8 m panel, the maximum is what fits a 6.62 m outer width. Wavelength 8.0 m: 1.5 waves per leg, half a wave over the top, an arc like Erne's rather than a serration. Phase 1/11 turn per truss: adjacent trusses differ by at most 0.17 m, and the crest line crosses the side elevation diagonally, which is the Tschumi effect. Rejected: a ripple in the inner chord too (the inner chord is what the box ties to and what stands on the shoe; it should be straight); a wave symmetric about the apex (kills the diagonal travel); amplitude 0.20 (a 0.4 m ripple on a 6.6 m elevation is 6 percent, hard to see).

**Inner outline as a 1:6 gable.** The ring's inner top chord follows the box roof at 0.07 clear, so the box roof and the ring have the same pitch. A flat inner chord would need a flat box roof with no fall. 1:6 is below the 1:3 threshold where ceiling ties stop being required, but the box roof trusses tie their heels anyway.

**Truss plane 120 mm thick, webs in two planes.** With one web plane (chord + 30 gap + chord) the two webs meeting at a node collide. A 60 mm gap gives the rising webs and the falling webs their own 30 mm plane, each nailed to the chord slat on its side. Rejected: gusseted nodes (no sheet material); lapping the webs (an extra joint type per node).

**Y-bracing in the gap.** The braces between ring legs cannot lie on the outer chord (it ripples) or inside the truss depth (webs). They lie flat on the legs' inner faces, in the 0.082 m gap between the box and the legs, as two X's per side with halving joints at the crossings and horizontal ties at the X ends. The red building's red diagonals sit in the same place relative to its box. Rejected: single tension diagonals per side (a compression diagonal 8.7 m long in a slat buckles, and the two sides would have to share load through the box); braces inside the truss depth (collide with webs).

**Door 1.00 x 2.10 with doubled jacks.** The module gives 1.12 clear between single jacks on the +/-0.65 kings; doubled jacks bring it to 1.00. Opening size follows the door, not the grid. Header of four slats on edge (120 x 120) for a 1.0 m span under a light roof. Rejected: the photo's squat 0.8 x 0.75 hatch (not a door); a header of paired slats only (60 wide, would not fill the stud zone and the cripples would land on nothing).

**Raft.** One concrete element, 7.20 x 7.20 x 0.25, top at the ground. It is the modelled ground, not a timber member. Rejected: pads under each truss foot plus a slab under the box (22 pads plus a slab, more elements for the same statement); no foundation (truss feet on nothing).

**Piece count.** About 3200 pieces, 1780 of them in the ring trusses. If the check loop cannot carry it, the panel length goes from 0.80 to 1.00 first; the truss count and module stay. Reported to CraftBot.

## Research round (v01)

**What the manuals settled.** Board spans (CMHC Tables 22 and 35, FRIM A7): both boards are conservative at 0.65 m. Heel bearing over the wall plate (CMHC Fig. 86). 1:6 is CMHC's low-slope threshold, so the box roof would need a membrane; not modelled by the brief's rule against sheet material. A 1.0 m door needs one jack per side; my doubled jacks are for the opening size, kept. Post base as a steel U-strap with two bolts (FRIM Sheet 7), named. Sleeper on slab over polyethylene (CMHC Fig. 47 B), named.

**What the manuals corrected.** Brace angle: CMHC and FRIM both want 45 degrees or steeper; my two X's per side across the whole 6.5 m row stood at 42 degrees. Changed to four X's per side in 3.25 m wide panels, 61 degrees, 16 diagonals in all. Rejected: three X's over the height across the full row (steeper is taller and narrower, so more panels over the height make it worse, 31 degrees); a single K per panel (a compression diagonal in a 30 mm slat over 6 m).

**What the manuals do not reach, and what I did instead.** No manual states 30 x 120 or 24 x 120 as structural members (FRIM's thinnest are 35 x 72 truss members); no stud table goes past 4.2 m (CMHC Table 25) against my 11.5 m; CMHC's minimum column is 140 x 140. The brief asks for thin slats, so these are departures by instruction, and the compensating devices are the ones in the concept: pairing, rails every 0.65 m on both faces, ties to the ring legs at every rail, and the trusses rather than the studs taking the wind. TRADA's 600 mm batten maximum against my 0.65 m rails: 50 mm over, kept for the one-module argument. The sandwich truss node and the clerestory band are extensions by analogy and are labelled so in concept 4. All of it goes into the rationale's deviation ledger under "outside the manuals".

**External search.** Approved one: a ledged-and-braced board door, because no manual names it. The leaf is a small element; the sizes in the concept are mine until the row lands and stay mine if the source disagrees only in millimetres.


## v01 Builder questions (2026-09-14, applies to v02 and later)

The v01 Builder found five places where a concept number contradicted the concept's own geometry and resolved each toward the checkable requirement, plus three open questions. My answers, with what lost. Concept numbers patched in place (sections 1, 3.2, 3.3.5, 3.3.6, 3.3.8, 3.5, 3.6), each patch marked "v01 derived constant" or "v02".

**1. Box roof end trusses at y = +/-1.89, confirmed.** The end wall's inner rail starts at 1.974 and its stud zone at 2.004; a 120 mm truss centred on 1.95 reaches 2.01 and cuts both. At 1.89 the outer slat face sits on the inner board plane. The truss still bears on the side wall head plate, which spreads the 60 mm offset from the stud pair at 1.95; the vertical-alignment rule is about load reaching a stud line, and a 60 mm eccentricity on a 120 mm plate over a 60 mm stud pair is within the plate. Lost: five trusses with the gable plate carrying the deck edge (deck span 0.76 at the ends breaks R-24's 0.65); moving the end walls out (changes the room, R-01).

**2. Deck eave at x = 2.249 and top chord tails at 2.22, confirmed.** My 2.28 was an arithmetic slip against my own leg inner face at 2.26. Nineteen whole 120 boards along a 1:6 slope give 2.249 in plan, no ripped board, 0.071 overhang past the wall face. The chord tails at 2.22 stay under the deck and clear the brace plane. Lost: legs moved out to 2.35 (changes W_out, every leg and the 2:1 tuning, for a 30 mm overhang).

**3. Brace plane at x = 2.230 to 2.260, confirmed.** The concept's sentence was right ("flat against the legs' inner faces") and its numbers wrong. The braces work only if they are nailed to every leg they cross, so contact is the rule and 2.198 to 2.228 was a typo. Clear of the wall face by 0.052; the box-to-leg ties are still named, not modelled.

**4. Upper tie at deck underside minus 10 mm (11.669 to 11.789), lower panel top at 6.07, confirmed.** The tie's job is to hold the top of the braced panel at the eave and tie the legs together there; 10 mm under the deck edge is as high as it gets without cutting the deck or the ring's corner mitre. Written as a rule, not a number, because z_h is tuned by the Builder. The 6.05 was another slip (20 mm overlap with the lower tie's top at 6.07). Lost: the deck pulled back to 2.22 to keep the tie at 11.75 (the deck would then overhang the wall by 42 mm and the tie would sit above the head plate for no reason).

**5. Splices, confirmed with one change.** The rule is now a number: splices on a rail centre (sill rail included) or a truss node, the two slats of a pair at least one module apart on studs and two panels apart on chords; "half a length" is gone. Side wall studs (A 4.55/9.10, B 2.60/7.15, stagger 1.95) and leg chords (A nodes 6/12, B nodes 4/10, stagger two panels) pass. The gable studs' third cut at the sill rail does not: it put the B splice at 9.57, 0.47 from the A splice at 9.10. B at 3.25/7.80 instead gives pieces 3.25, 4.55 and at most 4.37 m to the apex (deck underside 11.85 to 12.17), two splices per slat, stagger 1.30 from A, all on rails. Same set for the door cripples. Lost: the third cut (more pieces, less stagger); a B set at 3.90/8.45 (stagger 0.65, the minimum, when 1.30 is free).

**6. Outer chord corners mitred, confirmed; the depth floor stays at 0.33.** The offset-polygon vertex is the honest geometry of an offset polyline; the chamfer was a shortcut in my node rule that the wave exposed at eight of 22 eave corners. Raising the minimum depth to 0.50 (d = 0.75 +/- 0.25) would push the maximum to 1.00, W_out to about 6.76 and every tuned number with it, and would still leave a chamfered shoulder at the eave where the ring should read as a gable on legs. Structurally the corner vertex is a kink in the outer chord with no web to it, about 0.4 m from the adjacent outer vertices each way; the chord is a nailed sandwich pair and the kink is a mitre in both slats, so the deviation force at the kink goes into the two webs either side. Recorded as an unbraced kink, plausible at this scale, not calculated. Lost: a web to the corner vertex (no free web plane at a corner node).

**7. R-28 covers the y-bracing only.** CMHC Fig. 86 and FRIM Fig. 30 are about braces that stiffen a frame or a wall. ## Phase 2, structural review (2026-09-14, on v03, reference set aside)

Read from `version_notes.md` v01 to v03 and `inspection_v03.md`, not from the concept. The checklist of the structural-logic skill, item by item.

**1. Vertical load paths, as sentences.** Ring trusses: outer and inner chord pairs of every ring end on the raft at z = 0 at both feet (steel U-strap and two bolts named, FRIM Sheet 7, not modelled); webs between the chord slats carry the truss's own weight down both chords. Box roof: deck boards on the top chords of 7 sandwich trusses at 0.65 (end pair at +/-1.89), bottom chords on the side wall head plates over the full stud zone, head plates on paired studs at 0.65 (spliced one slat at a time on rail centres, partner continuous), studs on the bottom plate on the raft; the gable head plates carry the deck edge straight into the end wall studs. Door: header of four slats on doubled jacks on the plate. Floor: boards on joists lying on the raft. Braces and ties: nailed to the legs they cross. Every family closes to the raft; nothing floats (0 floating in v03).

**2. Lateral, per direction.** Across the trusses (x): 11 rings with trussed corners (the mitred outer vertex at each eave and the webs from the corner node to both neighbouring outer vertices make the corner a truss, so "portal" is earned, not assumed); the box is tied to the legs at rail levels (named). Each ring takes its own 0.65 m strip; no diaphragm needed. Along the row (y): the two braced planes at x = +/-2.245 (four X's per side at 59 to 61 degrees, ties at 6.0 and 11.6) from z 0.15 to 11.7; the box deck brings the end walls' wind to the side walls through the truss heels on the head plates, and the rails and ties bring it to the legs. The braced planes reach the eave. Above the upper tie the 11 ring tops (4.7 m arches, 1.4 m above the tie) are tied to nothing in y: each top run stands as a cantilever from its own braced legs. Finding, see 6.

**3. Bearing at seats, continuity.** Bottom chords on head plates for 0.12 (the stud zone); top chords seated on the bottom chord's arris at the heel; deck on chord tops across every truss; joists flat on the raft; truss feet square on the raft; header on jacks 0.12 each side; bottom plate and outer bottom rail continuous under the door (the threshold). Ring chord splices on nodes, two panels apart in a pair; stud splices on rail centres one module apart. Discontinuities walked: door (header, cripples), eave slot (the deck reaches the side wall only through the seven heels, a named nailed connection, fine for a diaphragm on a 4.3 m span), gable corners (four-slat corner post from the side head plate to the gable plate).

**4. Foundations.** The raft is the modelled ground; undersides irrelevant on flat ground. FRIM's 50 mm footing upstand under each truss foot and the polyethylene under the joists are not modelled (no terrain, no moisture in the vocabulary). Overturning of a 13.2 m tall, 6.6 m wide frame is held by the named hold-downs at 44 feet and a 31 t raft; not calculated, recorded.

**5. Sizes and restraint, the one real finding.** The sections are outside every manual and are recorded (R-32). What the model does not yet do is give the ring chords a weak-axis restraint. The inner leg chords are crossed by the braces and ties every 2.5 to 3 m, which is a restraint. The outer chords, 28 m of paired 30 mm slats per ring, are restrained out of their plane by nothing at all between the raft and the raft: the top run's outer chord is a compression chord under its own weight and under wind on the row, the leg's outer chord is in compression under wind from the far side, and a 30 x 120 slat pair with a 28 m unbraced length is a mechanism, not a member. The inner top chords over the roof are in the same state (no tie in y except through the legs). In a built Erne roof the purlins and the roof plane do this job; here the ripple forbids a straight purlin, but short spacers between adjacent trusses do not need to be straight across the row. Action: requirement P2-01, spacers F 30 x 120 between the chord faces of adjacent rings, at every third outer vertex along the outer chord (about every 2.4 m along the outline; each spacer runs between the two outer vertices at the same s, so it is inclined by the depth difference, at most 0.17 over 0.53) and at every inner node of the top runs (six per bay), nailed to both chord faces. About 120 outer and 60 inner pieces. Rejected: straight purlins over the outer chords (cannot lie on a rippling surface); nothing (the weak-axis length stays 28 m; the review exists to catch exactly this).

**6. Lateral in y above the tie.** With the spacers the 11 tops become a grid, and a grid without diagonals holds only by chord bending. Action: P2-02, one zigzag of diagonals per slope in the roof plane, F 30 x 120 laid flat in the 0.07 gap under the inner top chords (top face on the chord undersides, 0.04 clear of the deck), from the eave line to the apex line over three bays each (plan angle about 50 degrees; FRIM Sheet 9 puts its roof diagonal at 45), from truss 0 to truss 9 and its mirror so they form X's; bay 9 to 10 stays unbraced, the end truss being held by the spacers. 16 pieces of about 3.05 m. Rejected: diagonals on top of the outer chords (the ripple); diagonals under the deck inside the box (R-08, the inside stays plain).

**7. Details by gravity, sliding, moisture, racking.** Posts on the slab: shoes named, upstand not modelled. Roof drains at 1:6 to both eaves over the open eave slot and past the 0.08 gap; no gutter in the vocabulary, recorded. Halving joints thin each brace to 15 mm at the crossing; standard for slat X-bracing, kept. Racking of the box: two board faces on rails; kept.

**Considered and not changed.** The box roof trusses' 0.12 heel depth for a 4.25 m span (apex depth about 0.5, span/9, plausible for a light deck); the 0.24 m open eave slot (the diaphragm goes through the heels, not through boards); the porch bays' free trusses (braced by the same planes as the rest); the 60 x 120 studs at 11.3 m (restrained every 0.65 on both faces, and the wind is the rings' job, not theirs).

Closing line: every section is plausible for its span, none is calculated.
